olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $ABCD$ be circumscribed about a circle with all interior and exterior angles $\geq 60^\circ$. Prove $\frac{1}{3}|AB^3-AD^3|\leq|BC^3-CD^3|\leq 3|AB^3-AD^3|$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2004

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ are integers with $\gcd=1$. Set $S$ satisfies: (a) each $a_i\in S$; (b) $a_i-a_j\in S$; (c) if $x,y\in S$ and $x+y\in S$, then $x-y\in S$. Prove $S=\mathbb{Z}$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2004

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: For which real $k>0$ can a $1\times k$ rectangle be dissected into two similar, noncongruent polygons?
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2004

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Alice and Bob play on a $6\times 6$ grid. Each turn: player writes a rational not yet on the grid in an empty square. Alice goes first. When full, in each row the largest number is colored black. Alice wins if she can draw a path from top to bottom through black squares. Find a winning strategy.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2004

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Circle $\omega$ inscribed in $ABCD$ with center $I$. If $(AI+DI)^2+(BI+CI)^2=(AB+CD)^2$, prove $ABCD$ is an isosceles trapezoid.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2004
